On today's stock market crash:

As an investor, on days like today, you have to ask yourself one question: What fundamentally changed over the last 24 hours?

The shift in the fundamental backdrop cannot be attributed solely to the Midterm Election results; markets had already largely priced in the outcome.

So, what changed between yesterday and today? What is the fundamental reason for today's decline?

One of the most likely catalysts is growing concern about a potential "ban" on AI, or at the very least, severe regulation of the industry.

Over the last 24 hours, Democratic lawmakers have publicly called for restrictions on advanced AI development, including an outright "ban on artificial superintelligence."

Frankly, an outright ban will not happen.

Such a ban, if even possible to enforce, would effectively mean the US surrendering its position in the global AI race to China.

Does this mean AI is "over" or today's stock market crash marks "the end?" Absolutely not.

Rather, we believe we are witnessing a sudden shift in sentiment colliding with excessive levels of leverage, potentially triggering forced liquidations by several major institutional investors.

Therefore, today's downturn is more technical than fundamental. This is not to discount the concerns around regulation, they are legitimate. But price action right now does not look orderly or rational.

We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in human history.

Zoom out and remain calm.

posts.text:
Remember, remember the fifth of November,
 The chips and the AI rot.
 I see no reason the Nasdaq’s lean season
 Should ever be forgot.
Chips, chips, ’twas the market’s intent
To ride the blue wave clear past Parliament,
But six minutes in, the rally was spent,
And the Nasdaq slid into correction’s descent.
Voters said no to the data-center boom,
Congress turned blue, and traders saw doom;
They feared that the rules for AI would get tough,
And by mid-morning, two trillion had been sold off.
Nvidia, Broadcom, Micron, AMD,
Took a beating for all of the Street to see;
The SOX shed ten percent, a sight to behold,
While Bitcoin slipped under seventy-six thousand, we’re told.
Holler, boys, holler, boys, let the bells ring,
Oil ticked higher while tech took the sting.
Sell, boys, sell, boys, sell everything,
And God save the bid, wherever it’s hiding.
So remember, remember the fifth of November,
 The bid that the bulls never got.
 I see no reason why the fifth of November
 Should ever be forgot.
